name: Wildmane Cleansing
summary: In Mulgore, the tauren's cleansing work reaches its final well. Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village sends you north with the completed Wildmane Totem to cleanse the poisoned water and protect the tauren's way of life.

sections.title: Purifying the Earth Mother's Gift
sections.body:
Mulgore's wells sustain the herds, the soil, and the tauren tribes gathered around Thunder Bluff. The Venture Company and encroaching goblins have fouled them with toxic industrial runoff. The tauren elders see the danger to their people and their land.

The Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells are purified. Now the Wildmane Water Well remains, the third and final corrupted site. Its waters still need spiritual cleansing.

sections.title: The Wildmane Totem
sections.body:
The Wildmane Cleansing Totem is made from elements gathered across the region. It draws on the restoring power of ancestral spirits and elemental earth. Plant it beside the foul waters north of Thunder Bluff. The ritual disperses chemicals, draws out toxins, and revives the natural flow.

The cleansing guards the tauren against disease. It also makes clear they will not tolerate the despoiling of their sacred ground.

faq.q: Why was the Wildmane Water Well poisoned?
faq.answer: Goblin operations driven by industrial greed and logging enterprises poisoned Mulgore's underground waters with chemical waste. The waste threatens wildlife and tribal settlements.

faq.q: Where is the Wildmane Water Well located?
faq.answer: The Wildmane Water Well lies on the plains directly north of Thunder Bluff's towering mesas.
Mull Thunderhorn, an elder in Bloodhoof Village, guides you in making the totems and sends you to purify the wells.

faq.q: What other wells are part of this purification effort?
faq.answer: The Wildmane Well is the third of three vital water sources. The Winterhoof Water Well and Thunderhorn Water Well, both to the south, came first.

faq.q: How does the cleansing totem work?
faq.answer: Made with ancestral magic and purified natural elements, the totem channels restoring spiritual power into the water table to neutralize goblin pollutants.

faq.q: What does completing this ritual mean for Bloodhoof Village?
faq.answer: Cleansing all three wells secures safe drinking water for the tribes of central Mulgore. It honors the tauren duty to heal the Earth Mother from industrial exploitation.

angles.text: As a tauren, restoring Mulgore's three ancestral wells is a rite of passage. It proves your devotion to preserving the Earth Mother's gifts.
As a shaman, you use ritual totems to undo mechanical pollution and keep harmony between natural elements and living communities.
As a druid, you help reverse goblin destruction by healing blighted ecosystems and protecting Mulgore's pastures.
